projects.title: Global Health and Medical Humanities Initiative (GHMHI)
projects.description: The goal of the GHMHI is to provide MIT students the training to critically analyze the determinants of health and the role of medicine in society from cross-cultural, interdisciplinary perspectives. Professor Erica Caple James, Postdoctoral Associate Seth D. Hannah, and Administrative Assistant Brittany Peters of the MIT Anthropology Department are leading the initiative. My role was to research Global Health-related programs at other schools to understand their structures and objectives, then present my findings to the GHMHI faculty to propose a structure for the Global Health and Medical Humanities program at MIT.

projects.title: Magnetic Nanoparticles for Treatment of Metastatic Breast Cancer - Langer Laboratory
projects.description: The goal of this project is to develop a magnetic nanoparticle technology with the ability to selectively locate and attack breast cancer cells that have metastasized to areas difficult to reach with current technologies, such as the brain. My responsibilities included the optimization of the iron oxide nanoparticle synthesis protocol and the synthesis of the particles themselves. I modified chitosan with PEG, nucleated iron oxide cores, conjugated biological coatings to the nuclei, then adjust the protocol for future trials after analyzing polydispersity index and particle size data.

projects.title: Macrophage Response in Endometriosis - Lauffenburger Laboratory
projects.description: The overarching goal of this project was to analyze macrophage response in endometriosis. We want to determine how macrophage phenotypes, specifically the wound-healing phenotype, promote growth of endometriotic lesions. The three main phenotypes we examined were classical/microbicidal (which fight infection), wound-healing, and anti-inflammatory. In completing experimental data analysis, we aimed to gain a better understanding of what causes endometriosis and how it can be prevented.My role:• Isolated and differentiated macrophages from peripheral blood monocytes (U937 cell line, blood bank samples, clinical endometrial biopsies).• Used sandwich immunoassays to analyze how each phenotype promotes the growth of endometriotic lesions via the different released chemical signals and marker proteins.

Ran the SF half marathon this weekend! People ask if my legs are sore (they are) and if I had fun (I did). But the real joy wasn't just the race itself -- it came at the finish line. Aaron and John surprised me with great vibes and loud cheers. I spend a lot of time with them at work. We solve hard problems together, we push each other, all of that. But this weekend reminded me that the people I'm lucky enough to work alongside are also great humans and friends. The kind who show up on a Sunday morning for something that has nothing to do with work. Grateful for you both, Aaron and John. Can't wait for what's next.

When you're hiring someone at a startup, you want someone who's good at their job. But beyond that, you want a thought partner. Meet Inna . She's creative. She goes above and beyond. She's someone who makes you more willing to say the half-formed idea so you can hash it out together. Inna's energy isn't just positive. It's the kind that makes the room less afraid to think out loud. Most appreciation posts are really about output. What someone shipped, what they delivered, the tangible thing that shows up in a report. And that's worth celebrating for sure. But the person who gets others to show up with them? That's a different category of impact. Inna - thank you for making work better by making the people around you better at showing up :)

The best moments aren't at work. Or at least most of mine aren't. Last Friday, my team and I just hung out. No agenda, no standup, no roadmap. We ended up talking about the things that never quite fit between Slack threads: what we're chasing, our families, the goals that have nothing to do with any quarter. You can spend forty hours a week two desks from someone and still only know the version of them that shows up to meetings. The quiet moments are where you meet the people you work with. So before your next sync kicks off, try something: ask someone what they're genuinely excited about outside of all this. Then actually listen. (Pictured: my team, off the clock, just being their best selves.)

This is my last week at Peak XV Partners It’s hard to say goodbye to a place that has felt like home 🥹 As an immigrant, I’ve spent much of my life learning how to adapt to different rooms, which made this chapter especially meaningful. From day one, I could be 100% myself 💙 When I joined, I was the second employee in the US. Two years later, we’ve built a team, opened our SF office, activated a community of 100+ founders, and partnered with 30+ new companies in the region! 👊 As a lifelong startup operator who mostly experienced venture through quarterly board meetings 😄 this chapter completely changed how I think about it. I used to think venture was primarily about deploying capital — I mean, how hard could it be? 😂 Instead, I found a craft built on pattern recognition, conviction, long-term thinking, and most importantly, showing up for founders through the highs and lows of company building. I’m leaving with deep gratitude for my PeakXV teammates, the founders who trusted me, and the opportunity to learn across so many companies, industries, stages and regions. 🙏 A lot of people have asked why I’d leave something so special… Sometimes you don’t leave because you’re running away from something. You leave because you’re being pulled towards something Becoming a mom has been clarifying in ways I didn’t expect. And for me that pull is back to building. Back in the arena 💪 So here’s to listening to my heart, ignoring the noise in my brain, and continuing to run my own race 🏃‍♀️ LFG 🚀

Today marks the closing of one remarkable chapter and the opening of a new journey ahead. After nearly seven incredibly rewarding years at Breakthrough Energy , I'm excited to share I'll be joining WovenEarth Ventures as a Partner in September. It's difficult to capture what these past seven years have meant. One of the greatest privileges has been taking an idea and making it come to life - through building the Breakthrough Energy Fellows program, alongside an extraordinary team and global ecosystem of founders, universities, incubators, investors and industry partners. Together, we've supported more than 100 startups across six cohorts in 23 countries, helping exceptional founders move breakthrough science toward real-world impact. Those companies have gone on to raise more than $750 million in follow-on funding - a testament to the founders themselves and the power of an ecosystem willing to back bold ideas in their earliest stages. I'm deeply grateful to everyone who has been part of that journey, and especially to Bill Gates the founder of Breakthrough Energy, thank you for your leadership and deep curiosity continuing to push us all to seek out and scale these new innovations. To Rodi Guidero for his visionary leadership, partnership and commitment to scaling; to Eric Toone my mentor, teacher, and thought partner for his unwavering support, scientific leadership and commitment to support the innovations at the heart of this work; and to Carmichael Roberts for his coaching, supporting and cheering me on (front row) as I took on new opportunities during this journey. I am incredibly appreciative for everything this chapter has taught me, and I will carry those lessons with me as I begin the next one at WovenEarth Ventures. WovenEarth Ventures is as an investment platform delivering curated access into early-stage cleantech, through a strategic combination of fund investments and co-investments. I’m proud to be joining a firm that is both an investor in Breakthrough Energy Ventures and a collaborator across the broader ecosystem. While my role is changing, my mission remains steadfast. My focus will continue working to identify and support exceptional founders and fund managers that are focused on advancing transformative technologies needed to accelerate the energy and industrial transition. I leave Breakthrough Energy with enormous gratitude for the AMAZING team and friendships that have developed over this time - and tremendous excitement for what collaborations come next. Benjamin Gaddy Meghan Bader Brenda Haendler John Lemmon Jolene Gurevich Saad Chaudhry Taylor Carvalho Karp Matt Purdy Terence Tse Rosemary Cox-Galhotra Abigail Mathieson Malik Jane Zhang Lastly, thank you to my family, and those in my personal boardroom (you know who you are) for cheering me on at every chapter! And Chicago friends and community - I'm not going anywhere, I will still be based here, please let's collaborate on this new adventure. #BELIEVE

I'm hiring a Chief of Staff at Lydian. This role comes with big shoes to fill: Amanda Ritter has set the standard for the role over the last 2 years and has now been promoted to set up and lead permanent communications and policy functions as our Head of Corporate Affairs. The new Chief of Staff will help us maintain operational excellence during a major inflection point for the company. This person will help us keep commercial, technology, and finance in lockstep while growing the team rapidly; will steward our iconoclastic spirit while making sure we have the foundations for safe, disciplined commercialization of our technology; and will help position us for changing market realities. The CoS will take on special projects across commercial, finance, new product development, or other areas. The right fit probably has an engineering or similar technical background.
